correctness.rationale: For each even m>=4, K=I+11^T maps any balanced sign vector s to itself. With z±=π1±δs, h sinδ=2δ (unique 0<δ<π for h>2) gives exact prime-two exchange. Both Jacobians are I−h cosδ K, with eigenvalues 1−h cosδ (m−1 times) and 1−(m+1)h cosδ. Squared two-return eigenvalues are <1 exactly for δ_m<δ<π/2, where (m+1)δ_m cotδ_m=1, equivalently h_m<h<π. At h_m or π a unit multiplier precludes strict linear attraction; for h>π the branch repels. Signs modulo s↔−s count C(m,m/2)/2 distinct cycles, with disjoint local basins. IFT continues each hyperbolic cycle for small positive edge-weight perturbations at fixed m,h. From δ_m=π/2−2/[π(m+1)]+O(m^-2) one obtains π−h_m=4/[π(m+1)]+O(m^-2). Not all cycles are classified.
residual_risks: Finite independent checks do not prove the all-parameter claims; analytic arguments or exhaustive certificates are required.

value.rationale: A shared sharp stability window supporting C(m,m/2)/2 distinct attracting period-two star-network states is a motivated dynamical phenomenon, exponentially growing in leaf count and robust to individual edge-weight perturbations. It is not merely a finite numerical observation or renaming of the small-step theorem. The result establishes this explicit family, not global enumeration.
residual_risks: No claim that all period-two cycles are captured.
Boundary equal-multiplier nonlinear stability and uniform-in-m heterogeneity tolerance remain open.
